subject: Forensic log validation & confirmation — no customer data exposure
messages:
From: Tanya Rao <tanya.rao@globexpayments.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: security@globexpayments.com
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Strange spike — please confirm any customer data movement

Evelyn —

We detected an anomalous outbound pattern from one of our integration endpoints around 08/28 02:12 UTC. No clear data payloads were visible on our side but the traffic was unusual and we need confirmation that no customer PII or transaction data left Redwood's systems as a result.

Can you share the results of any log scans or forensic checks you run? Ben Turner from our third-party audit team is copied. We need a written confirmation for our compliance team.

Thanks,
Tanya Rao
Head of Security Operations
Globex Payments
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Tanya Rao <tanya.rao@globexpayments.com>
Cc: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com, chloe_martin@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Strange spike — please confirm any customer data movement

Tanya — thanks for flagging this. We started an immediate triage as soon as you reported the anomaly. High level: we have not seen evidence of data exfiltration in preliminary checks, but we are running targeted forensic scans across the data plane and request/response logs to be thorough.

What we're doing now:
- Running full request-trace reconstruction for the 02:00–02:30 UTC window (per-request IDs).
- Cross-checking our KV and prefix cache access logs against S3/object-store egress logs.
- Exporting TLS session metadata and DLP detection hits (if any).
- Performing a content-level search of any stored request/response bodies in the retention window.

I will share the scan summary and evidence bundle as soon as the forensic scan completes — aiming within 36 hours. Attaching a short checklist of the queries we will run.

Attachment: kibana-query-list-GLB-20260828.txt (query list)

Evelyn Hart
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
evelyn_hart@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0124
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 09:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: initial log sweep results for GLB alert (08/28)

Eve / Chloe —

Quick internal update before we send to the customer: I ran the scripts listed in the kibana query list across the ingestion cluster, model-serving nodes, and the S3 access logs for the window 2026-08-28T02:00:00Z to 2026-08-28T02:45:00Z. Findings so far:
- No abnormal get/put patterns to public S3 buckets. Outbound egress shows standard control-plane telemetry and a small number of health-check connections to our metrics endpoint.
- KV cache access shows reads consistent with expected traffic for the customer’s route; no large sequential reads that would indicate bulk dump.
- No DLP hits on request bodies indexed (DLP engine scanned request payloads with sha256ed artifact matching; zero matches).
- Identified one repeated client IP (internal NAT) that made multiple short requests — likely a retry loop from a partner integration; requests contain only identifiers (hashed ids) and no full PII payloads.

Next steps: generate the evidence bundle with per-request timelines, the S3 access logs, and the query output. I can assemble a redacted PDF summary for the customer and hand off the full CSV evidence (sha256 checksums included) to Ben if they request it.

Sergio
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Tanya Rao <tanya.rao@globexpayments.com>
Cc: Ben Turner <ben.turner@auditors.io>, sergio_alvarez@redwood.com, chloe_martin@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Forensic log validation & confirmation — no customer data exposure

Tanya / Ben —

We completed the forensic validation for the 2026-08-28 02:00–02:30 UTC window. Summary conclusions (executive):
- No customer PII or transaction data was transmitted from Redwood systems during the timeframe in question.
- There are no signs of bulk data transfer or sustained egress activity consistent with data extraction.
- All request/response bodies that existed in the retention window were scanned by our DLP process; no matches found.

What we examined (technical):
- Per-request trace reconstruction using request IDs provided by Globex and our proxy logs.
- Backend service access logs and KV cache read/write histories.
- Object-store (S3) access logs and internal egress controls (signed URLs, referrer, ACL checks).
- TLS session metadata, including ciphers and endpoints, to validate no proxying to third parties.
- DLP scan output for request bodies and stored artifacts.

Evidence provided: attached is a redacted forensic summary (forensic-log-scan-summary-20260830.pdf) that includes a timeline, query outputs, and hash digests of the exported logs. For privacy we redacted full request bodies; the unredacted CSV evidence bundle is available by secure link below upon execution of an NDA/POA if Globex requires raw artifacts for audit.

We are confident in the no-exfiltration conclusion based on the above checks and the SHA256 digests of each evidence file. If you would like, we can schedule a short call with Sergio to walk through the technical artifacts.

Attachments: forensic-log-scan-summary-20260830.pdf; kibana-query-list-GLB-20260828.txt
Evidence link: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/forensic/GLB-20260828-logs

Requested next steps from Globex:
- Confirm whether you need the unredacted evidence bundle for your audit team (we will require standard access controls).
- If accepted, provide preferred date for a 30-minute technical review.

Thanks — glad we could close this quickly. Please reply with any follow-up questions or confirm that this note satisfies Globex compliance.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
